info.description:
XHTML2PDF ========= **Write the document in HTML and CSS. Get a PDF.** Pure Python on top of ReportLab, with no browser to install or keep running. .. image:: https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/xhtml2pdf?label=PyPI&logo=PyPI&logoColor=white&color=blue :target: https://pypi.python.org/pypi/xhtml2pdf :alt: PyPI version .. image:: https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/xhtml2pdf?label=Python&logo=Python&logoColor=white :target: https://www.python.org/downloads :alt: Python versions .. image:: https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/tests.yml?branch=master&label=Tests&logo=github&logoColor=white :target: https://github.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/actions/workflows/tests.yml :alt: Tests .. image:: https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/linting.yml?branch=master&label=Linting&logo=github&logoColor=white :target: https://github.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/actions/workflows/linting.yml :alt: Linting .. image:: https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/spelling.yml?branch=master&label=Spelling&logo=github&logoColor=white :target: https://github.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/actions/workflows/spelling.yml :alt: Spelling .. image:: https://img.shields.io/coveralls/github/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf?label=Coveralls&logo=Coveralls&logoColor=white :target: https://coveralls.io/github/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf :alt: Coveralls .. image:: https://img.shields.io/readthedocs/xhtml2pdf?label=Read%20the%20Docs&logo=read%20the%20docs&logoColor=white :target: http://xhtml2pdf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/?badge=latest :alt: Read the Docs xhtml2pdf turns HTML5 and CSS into PDF on top of the ReportLab toolkit. Anyone who can build a web page can build an invoice, a report, a ticket or a book with it, from a Django or Flask template or from a plain string, and render it anywhere Python runs. Made with xhtml2pdf =================== Every page below is an HTML document converted by xhtml2pdf, fonts, charts, barcodes and all. .. |annual-report| image:: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/master/docs/source/_static/readme/annual-report.png :width: 180px :alt: An annual report with a cover photo, key figures and charts .. |invoice| image:: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/master/docs/source/_static/readme/invoice.png :width: 180px :alt: An invoice with a long table of line items and totals .. |book| image:: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/master/docs/source/_static/readme/book.png :width: 180px :alt: The cover of a novella, a full-page illustration with the title .. |poster| image:: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/master/docs/source/_static/readme/poster.png :width: 180px :alt: A concert poster with a city skyline and a strip of dates .. |certificate| image:: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/master/docs/source/_static/readme/certificate.png :width: 180px :alt: A certificate of completion in landscape with a QR code .. |receipt-pos| image:: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/master/docs/source/_static/readme/receipt-pos.png :width: 180px :alt: A narrow point-of-sale receipt in a monospaced font .. |boarding-pass| image:: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/master/docs/source/_static/readme/boarding-pass.png :width: 180px :alt: An airline boarding pass with a barcode and a QR code .. |event-ticket| image:: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xhtml2pdf/xhtml2pdf/master/docs/source/_static/readme/event-ticket.png :width: 180px :alt: A concert ticket with a stub and a barcode +-----------------+-----------------+-----------------+-----------------+ | |annual-report| | |invoice| | |book| | |poster| | +-----------------+-----------------+-----------------+-----------------+ | |certificate| | |receipt-pos| | |boarding-pass| | |event-ticket| | +-----------------+-----------------+-----------------+-----------------+ Quick start =========== .. code:: bash pip install xhtml2pdf[all] .. code:: python from xhtml2pdf import pisa html = """

Hello, PDF

Written in HTML, laid out by CSS.

Page of
""" with open("hello.pdf", "wb") as output: result = pisa.CreatePDF(html, dest=output) print("errors:", result.err) Or from the command line: .. code:: bash xhtml2pdf report.html report.pdf What it can do ============== **Layout** * Flexbox (``display: flex``), including containers that break across pages, and ``display: inline-block``. * ``position: relative``, ``absolute`` and ``fixed``, with ``z-index``. * Block boxes with padding, borders and backgrounds around everything they hold, ``border-radius`` on blocks, tables, cells, images and inline boxes, and dashed, dotted and double borders. * Tables with header rows repeated on every page, ``colspan`` and ``rowspan``, auto margins and widths, and rows taller than a page cut between pages. * Word breaking with ``overflow-wrap``, ``page-break-before``/``after``, ``page-break-inside: avoid`` and keeping a heading with what follows. **CSS** * Selectors up to Level 4: ``:not()``, ``:is()``, ``:where()``, ``:has()``, ``:nth-child()`` and attribute selectors. * Custom properties with ``var()``, ``em``/``rem``/percent units, and colours with an alpha channel. * ``@font-face`` with TrueType and OpenType fonts, matched per character, so a paragraph that mixes scripts finds a font for each of them. **Pages** * ``@page`` sizes and margins, named page templates and left/right pages, background images, and frames for headers, footers and columns. * Page numbers and page counts, watermarks and backgrounds from an image or another PDF. **Navigation** * Tables of contents with dot leaders, more than one per document, clickable entries and a PDF outline (bookmarks). * Links to any element by ``id``, to other files and to the web. **International text** * Right-to-left documents in Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu, laid out with a pure-Python implementation of the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm that passes the whole of the Unicode conformance suites. * Chinese, Japanese and Korean, Cyrillic and Greek, with the document's language written to the PDF. **Graphics and PDF features** * SVG images, bar, line and pie charts, and barcodes and QR codes. * Fillable form fields, encryption with passwords and permissions, and digital signatures (simple and PAdES) through pyHanko. **Safe by default** * A document cannot read local files outside its directory or reach internal network addresses, and ``ResourceAccessPolicy.server()`` adds limits on size, nesting and time for HTML from untrusted sources. See `Security `__. Documentation ============= The documentation is on `Read the Docs `__, and what changed in each version is in the `Release Notes `__. Help improving it is welcome; a good place to start is ``docs/source/quickstart.rst``. Installation ============ .. code:: bash pip install xhtml2pdf[all] Python 3.10 and newer is tested and supported. Every mandatory requirement is listed in ``pyproject.toml`` and installed with xhtml2pdf; ``all`` adds the optional ones: pyHanko, for digital signatures, which is also the ``signing`` extra on its own. ``pip install xhtml2pdf`` leaves it out: asking for a signature then raises an ``ImportError`` that names the extra. ReportLab needs a rendering backend to turn vector graphics into bitmaps (for charts and SVG rasterised into the page). The supported one is `cairo `__, installed system-wide, for example through the OS package manager, together with the ``pycairo`` extra: .. code:: bash pip install xhtml2pdf[pycairo] The ``renderpm`` extra is a deprecated alias for ``pycairo``: ReportLab 5 removed the C ``RenderPM`` backend. See the `ReportLab installation notes `__. Development environment ======================= ``make devsetup`` creates ``.venv``, installs xhtml2pdf in editable mode with the ``test``, ``docs`` and ``release`` extras and installs the pre-commit hooks: .. code:: bash make devsetup source .venv/bin/activate Or by hand: .. code:: bash python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate pip install -e .[test,docs,release] Running tests ============= .. code:: bash make test # unit tests make test-ref # reference renders for testrender make test-render # compare the renders against the reference make test-browser # compare against a headless browser's rendering make test-all # every supported Python and ReportLab, with tox ``testrender/`` renders a set of documents and compares the pages; the browser comparison scores xhtml2pdf against Chrome on the same markup, so a change that moves a layout away from a browser's shows up as a regression. ``tools/perf`` measures time and memory. Contributing ============ This project is community-led. Ideas, bug reports with a small HTML that shows the problem, and pull requests are welcome on GitHub. If xhtml2pdf is useful to you, look at the `test coverage `__ for parts that are not yet tested. You can also support the project on `Patreon `__ or with Bitcoin: ``bc1qmr0skzwx5scyvh2ql28f7gfh6l65ua250qv227``. **Big thanks** to everyone who has worked on this project so far and to those who help maintain it. Alternatives ============ `WeasyPrint `__ covers much of the same ground with a different design and set of features. History ======= These are the major milestones and the maintainers of the project: * 2000-2007 Dirk Holtwick (commercial project of spirito.de) * 2007-2010 Dirk Holtwick (project named "pisa", project released as GPL) * 2010-2012 Dirk Holtwick (project named "xhtml2pdf", changed license to Apache) * 2012-2015 Chris Glass (@chrisglass) * 2015-2016 Benjamin Bach (@benjaoming) * 2016-2018 Sam Spencer (@LegoStormtroopr) * 2018-Current Luis Zarate (@luisza) For more history, see the `Release Notes `__.
